I checked the draft sentence by sentence against the brand policy.

- "New tins just landed for winter." This is a product fact (new products arriving), which the product team checks and which is fine as written. It is also not false urgency.
- "Deep green, gold lettering, and the same plastic-free tea bags inside." This is description of the tin. The plastic-free point is on the allowlist.
- "Our tea bags are plastic-free and home compostable." This matches the approved claim word for word, backed by the EN 13432 supplier certificate.

Channel: this is the brand's own Instagram account, so no "Ad" label is needed. There is no creator, gifted item or affiliate link.

Style: the tone is warm, plain and unhurried. It uses no banned words and no AI clichés, and the spelling is fine for UK English. One optional polish note: "plastic-free tea bags" appears twice in three short sentences, so the repetition could be trimmed (for example, drop "and the same plastic-free tea bags inside" or cut the last sentence). That is not a reason to hold it.

No unsupported claims, health claims, green claims beyond the allowlist, guarantees, urgency or missing labels. Approver per policy is Sam, so it needs his sign-off as with all public content.
